Large-scale health data
My collaborative work includes the analysis of large electronic health record and health-system datasets to address clinical and public health questions.
I have worked with network and PCORnet data on questions related to obesity, chronic disease, health-care delivery, and clinical outcomes.

title: Research & Applied Work
text:
Obesity and cardiometabolic health
A major area of my applied work is obesity care and the use of real-world health data to understand obesity treatment and related health outcomes.
Recent projects have examined obesity care in large academic health systems and patterns of weight classification and cardiometabolic diagnoses.

I provide statistical collaboration through the University of Pittsburgh Clinical and Translational Science Institute.
From 2023–2026, I served as a statistical consultant and analyst on multiple new and continuing CTSI BERD requests each year.

title: Can quantum-mechanical description of physical reality be considered complete?
text:
Abstract
In a complete theory there is an element corresponding to each element of reality. A sufficient condition for the reality of a physical quantity is the possibility of predicting it with certainty, without disturbing the system. In quantum mechanics in the case of two physical quantities described by non-commuting operators, the knowledge of one precludes the knowledge of the other. Then either (1) the description of reality given by the wave function in quantum mechanics is not complete or (2) these two quantities cannot have simultaneous reality. Consideration of the problem of making predictions concerning a system on the basis of measurements made on another system that had previously interacted with it leads to the result that if (1) is false then (2) is also false. One is thus led to conclude that the description of reality as given by a wave function is not complete.

title: Teaching Resources
text:
I develop open-access materials and interactive tools for learning introductory biostatistics and R. I have created these resources for use in class to demonstrate statistical concepts and outside of class for students to review concepts, practice coding, and explore additional examples.


Interactive demonstrations and practice activities designed to help students build intuition for foundational biostatistical concepts. The site includes visualizations, simulations, and interactive examples that students can use to explore statistical ideas and see how changing data or assumptions affects the results.
Visit my Intro Biostatistics Resources



Interactive R coding exercises designed to give students additional practice applying the programming skills used in introductory biostatistics. The activities focus on common tasks such as working with data, calculating summary statistics, creating visualizations, and applying basic statistical methods.
Visit my Coding Practice Resources
